claims.text: The starting material is equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr in the as-cast condition.
As-cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
HfNbTaTiZr has inadequate oxidation resistance for high-temperature use in air.
Pre-oxidizing the alloy in low-partial-pressure oxygen at 800–900 °C for 1–2 hours will create a thin oxide barrier.
The pre-oxidation treatment will produce a stable and adherent oxide scale.
The protective scale will be formed from constituent elements of HfNbTaTiZr.
The preformed oxide film will suppress subsequent oxidation kinetics and reduce oxygen pickup.
Pre-oxidized samples will have significantly better oxidation resistance than untreated samples.
After treatment and exposure, the alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature elongation.
After treatment and exposure, the alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The protective effect will remain effective in air at up to 1000 °C for 10–100 hours and at tensile strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr exposed under the same conditions lacks a protective oxide film.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr embrittles and loses mechanical integrity during the specified air exposure.
Anti-oxidation coatings or further composition modification are required for high-temperature use of this refractory alloy family in air.
Thermal cycling or overly prolonged exposure may degrade the integrity of the oxide scale.
The optimum pre-oxidation temperature and time require experimental validation.

contradictions.description: The 8–16% ductility target is defined as a room-temperature property, but the experiment proposes in situ elevated-temperature tension and then applies the same 8–16% value as a high-temperature ductility acceptance target.
